claims.title: Discovery of Toumaï
claims.summary: A team led by Michel Brunet recovered the cranium of Sahelanthropus tchadensis at the Toros-Menalla (TM 266) site in the Djurab desert; the species was announced in 2002 and dated to about seven million years.

sources.label: Sahelanthropus tchadensis: Ten Years After the Discovery

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-2001-discovery-of-toumai, claim TL:TCD:event:2001:discovery-of-toumai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Sao culture
claims.summary: The Sao settled the lower Chari and southern Lake Chad, producing celebrated terracotta and bronze figures across more than 350 known sites before being absorbed by later states.

sources.label: The Ancient Sao Civilization in Central Africa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-600bce-rise-of-the-sao-culture, claim TL:TCD:event:600bce:rise-of-the-sao-culture, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hummay founds the Sayfawa dynasty
claims.summary: Mai Hummay, the first Muslim ruler of Kanem, displaced the Duguwa and founded the Sayfawa (Sefuwa) dynasty, which would rule the empire for some seven centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1075-hummay-founds-the-sayfawa-dynasty, claim TL:TCD:event:1075:hummay-founds-the-sayfawa-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zenith under Dunama Dibalemi
claims.summary: Mai Dunama Dibalemi brought Kanem to its peak, projecting power from the Fezzan to the southern savanna and deepening trade and diplomatic ties with North Africa and Egypt.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1210-zenith-under-dunama-dibalemi, claim TL:TCD:event:1210:zenith-under-dunama-dibalemi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sayfawa flee Kanem for Bornu
claims.summary: Pressed by the Bulala, the Sayfawa abandoned Njimi and re-established the state in Bornu, west of Lake Chad, later founding the capital Ngazargamu.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1380-sayfawa-flee-kanem-for-bornu, claim TL:TCD:event:1380:sayfawa-flee-kanem-for-bornu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Golden age under Idris Alooma
claims.summary: Mai Idris Alooma modernised the army with Ottoman firearms and advisers and promoted Islamic law, leading Kanem-Bornu to its second peak.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1571-golden-age-under-idris-alooma, claim TL:TCD:event:1571:golden-age-under-idris-alooma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: End of the Sayfawa line
claims.summary: The traditional office of mai was abolished in 1846 after the al-Kanemi shehus, who had risen during the Fulani jihad, took full control of Bornu.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1846-end-of-the-sayfawa-line, claim TL:TCD:event:1846:end-of-the-sayfawa-line, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Wadai Sultanate
claims.summary: Abd al-Karim led an Islamic revolt that overthrew the Tunjur and established the Wadai (Ouaddaï) sultanate east of Lake Chad, ruled from Abéché.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1635-founding-of-the-wadai-sultanate, claim TL:TCD:event:1635:founding-of-the-wadai-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wadai's commercial expansion
claims.summary: Under Muhammad Sabun, Wadai expanded and prospered by controlling caravan routes from Abéché north to Benghazi and the east-west trade between Darfur and Bornu.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1804-wadai-s-commercial-expansion, claim TL:TCD:event:1804:wadai-s-commercial-expansion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Baguirmi and the slave trade
claims.summary: The sultanate of Baguirmi, Islamic from the sixteenth century, supplied large numbers of captives to the trans-Saharan slave trade alongside skins, ivory and cotton.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1600-baguirmi-and-the-slave-trade, claim TL:TCD:event:1600:baguirmi-and-the-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rabih conquers Bornu
claims.summary: Rabih az-Zubayr overran the Kanem-Bornu lands with one of the best-equipped armies in sub-Saharan Africa, ruling the basin as a military dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1893-rabih-conquers-bornu, claim TL:TCD:event:1893:rabih-conquers-bornu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Kousséri
claims.summary: Converging French columns defeated and killed Rabih near the Chari River; the French commander Major Lamy also fell, ending Rabih's empire and opening the basin to France.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1900-battle-of-kousseri, claim TL:TCD:event:1900:battle-of-kousseri, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chad joins French Equatorial Africa
claims.summary: France organised the conquered territory and incorporated Chad into the federation of French Equatorial Africa, governing the south far more closely than the Muslim north.

sources.label: Chad — Independence, Civil War, Lake Chad

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1910-chad-joins-french-equatorial-africa, claim TL:TCD:event:1910:chad-joins-french-equatorial-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autonomous republic proclaimed
claims.summary: Chad became an autonomous republic within the French Community, a step toward the full independence achieved in 1960.

sources.label: Chad — Independence, Civil War, Lake Chad

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1958-autonomous-republic-proclaimed, claim TL:TCD:event:1958:autonomous-republic-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence under Tombalbaye
claims.summary: Chad gained full independence from France, with François Tombalbaye as first president; his southern-centred, authoritarian rule soon stoked northern grievances.

sources.label: Chad — Independence, Civil War, Lake Chad

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-under-tombalbaye, claim TL:TCD:event:1960:independence-under-tombalbaye, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: FROLINAT and the civil war
claims.summary: The National Liberation Front of Chad (FROLINAT) launched an insurgency rooted in northern and Muslim discontent, beginning decades of civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1966-frolinat-and-the-civil-war, claim TL:TCD:event:1966:frolinat-and-the-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup kills Tombalbaye
claims.summary: Tombalbaye was assassinated in a military coup; General Félix Malloum took power but could not end the conflict with FROLINAT's factions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1975-coup-kills-tombalbaye, claim TL:TCD:event:1975:coup-kills-tombalbaye, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Habré seizes power
claims.summary: Hissène Habré captured N'Djamena and made himself president, establishing a repressive regime amid continuing war and Libyan intervention.

sources.label: Chad — Independence, Civil War, Lake Chad

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1982-habre-seizes-power, claim TL:TCD:event:1982:habre-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Toyota War with Libya
claims.summary: Chadian forces under Hassan Djamous won a string of victories at Fada, Bir Kora and Ouadi Doum, driving the Libyan army back toward the disputed Aouzou Strip.

sources.label: Chad and Libya: The Impact of the Great Toyota War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1987-the-toyota-war-with-libya, claim TL:TCD:event:1987:the-toyota-war-with-libya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Idriss Déby seizes power
claims.summary: Leading the Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS) from Sudan, Déby overthrew Habré and installed himself as president, beginning a thirty-year rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1990-idriss-deby-seizes-power, claim TL:TCD:event:1990:idriss-deby-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ awards Aouzou Strip to Chad
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that the disputed Aouzou Strip belonged to Chad; Libyan forces withdrew by the end of May 1994.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-1994-icj-awards-aouzou-strip-to-chad, claim TL:TCD:event:1994:icj-awards-aouzou-strip-to-chad, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Habré convicted of crimes against humanity
claims.summary: The Extraordinary African Chambers in Senegal sentenced Hissène Habré to life for crimes against humanity, war crimes and torture, a landmark of universal jurisdiction; the verdict was upheld on appeal in 2017.

sources.label: Hissène Habré convicted: a historic verdict for the victims

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-2016-habre-convicted-of-crimes-against-humanity, claim TL:TCD:event:2016:habre-convicted-of-crimes-against-humanity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Idriss Déby; son takes power
claims.summary: Déby died of wounds from fighting on the front line; a military council named his son, General Mahamat Idriss Déby, transitional president, widely seen as an unconstitutional succession.

sources.label: Mahamat Idriss Déby, son of slain president, emerges as Chad's new strongman

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Chad: From Toumaï and the Sahel empires to the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/TCD/chronicle#ev-2021-death-of-idriss-deby-son-takes-power, claim TL:TCD:event:2021:death-of-idriss-deby-son-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
